script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. SMALL-TOWN AMERICA - DAY

A picturesque town nestled in the rolling hills. CRICKETS CHIRP. SUN glints off SUNFLOWERS.

CUT TO:

EXT. MILLTOWN FACTORY - DAY

A bustling, old-fashioned factory. EMPLOYEES in blue overalls mill around.

INT. MILLTOWN FACTORY - BOILER ROOM - DAY

JIM, a seasoned foreman with a salt-and-pepper beard, tinkers with a boiler. His NEPHEW, MARC, a green newcomer, watches nervously.

JIM
(leaning on wrench)
You know, Marc, this boiler's been here since the turn of the century. It's got character, don't you think?

MARC
(sweating)
Sure, Uncle Jim. But what if it explodes?

JIM
(laughs)
It won't. We'll keep an eye on it.

CUT TO:

INT. MILLTOWN FACTORY - OFFICE - DAY

ELLEN, a stern, no-nonsense manager, examines a spreadsheet. BOB, a friendly but forgetful worker, enters.

ELLEN
(looking up)
Bob. I'm moving you to the boiler room.

BOB
(perplexed)
The boiler room? But I've worked in shipping for years!

ELLEN
(stern)
The company's restructuring. We need to save costs.

BOB
(sighs)
Alright, I'll give it a shot.

CUT TO:

EXT. MILLTOWN FACTORY - YARD - NIGHT

Jim and Marc work late. They talk about their dreams. Jim's is to retire and travel. Marc's is to move away and become a chef.

MARC
(pensive)
I just want something more, you know?

JIM
(smiling)
We all do, kid. Keep dreaming.

Sudden LOUD BANG.

CUT TO:

INT. MILLTOWN FACTORY - BOILER ROOM - NIGHT

Marc and Jim rush over to the boiler. Steam billows from a cracked pipe. The room starts to FILL WITH SMOKE.

MARC
(shouting)
Get everyone out!

Jim and Marc work together to shut off the power. They usher their coworkers to safety.

CUT TO:

EXT. MILLTOWN FACTORY - YARD - NIGHT

Emergency responders arrive. The factory is evacuated. Jim and Marc stand together, relieved and shaken.

JIM
(hugging Marc)
You did good today, kid.

MARC
(smiling)
Thanks, Uncle Jim.

CUT TO:

INT. MILLTOWN FACTORY - OFFICE - DAY

Ellen looks at the damage. Bob enters, visibly shaken.

ELLEN
(softening)
We all did good today. We're a team.

BOB
(teary-eyed)
Yeah, we are.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
